[Context: whose livelihoods are land-based. These strategies may include resettlement on public]
land (see footnote 1 above), or on private land acquired or purchased for resettlement.

Whenever replacement land is offered, resettles' are provided with land for which a

combination of productive potential, locational advantages, and other factors is at least

equivalent to the advantages of the land taken. If land is not the preferred option of the

displaced persons, the provision of land would adversely affect the sustainability of a

park or protected area, 17 or sufficient land is not available at a reasonable price, non-

land-based options built around opportunities for employment or self-employment

should be provided in addition to cash compensation for land and other assets lost. The

lack of adequate land must be demonstrated and documented to the satisfaction of the

Bank.

12. Payment of cash compensation for lost assets may be appropriate where (a) livelihoods
